subject: Committed GPU pool pricing and invoicing — monthly vs annual prepay options

Subject: Committed GPU pool quote request (monthly vs annual prepay)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran some internal sizing and we think Dataslice.ai will need a dedicated GPU pool to support model inference: roughly 40 concurrent streams at p50 latency target 120ms for a 2k token average, ~12M tokens/day expected over the first 3 months.

Before we move to a formal SOW, procurement asked for:
- A concise pricing comparison: monthly reserved vs annual prepay (deltas in discounts, invoicing cadence)
- True-up mechanics (how and when you reconcile usage vs commit)
- Overage rates and any per-token or per-GPU caps we can include to limit exposure
- PO process, invoice cadence, and typical Net terms (Net-30/Net-45)
- Throughput guarantees (how you define the committed throughput and how we measure violations)

I've attached a draft SOW and a high-level usage profile. Can you loop in pricing/finance and send a clean write-up? We prefer a single PO per contract and standard enterprise terms where possible.

Best,
Sanjay
VP Engineering, Dataslice.ai

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the details and the SOW. High-level options (quick summary):

1) Monthly reserved commit (no long-term prepay)
   - You commit X GPUs / throughput per month. Billed monthly for committed units.
   - True-ups: monthly reconciliation; if usage > commit, overage billed at 1.6x the committed unit rate.
   - No prepayment discount; flexibility to change commit month-to-month with 30-day notice.

2) Annual prepay (12-month contract)
   - Prepay the committed capacity for 12 months up-front (or 12 monthly invoices billed as prepay).
   - Discount tiers: 10% at 12-month, 7% at 6-month equivalent; additional volume > 100 GPUs negotiable.
   - True-ups: quarterly reconciliation with credit for underutilization applied to future quarter.
   - Overage: lower rate than monthly (1.2x committed unit rate) when prepay is selected.

Notes: throughput guarantees are measured at a per-route 99th percentile across a 30-day window; if we miss SLO by >3% we issue service credits per SLA. For PO/terms: we accept a single PO referencing the contract, standard Net-30; finance can permit Net-45 for enterprise PO.

Looping in Marissa and Rishi to add invoice schedule details and sample clauses. I'll also attach our pricing worksheet.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Adding an invoice-level breakdown and mechanics so procurement has something to give legal/finance:

Monthly reserved commit (option A) — mechanics:
- Invoice issued on day 1 of the month for the committed capacity at list rates.
- True-up: end-of-month usage report; overages invoiced on next month invoice.
- Credits: if usage < commit we do not apply negative invoices; customer may decrease commit with 30 days notice (prorated).
- PO: single monthly PO ok; Net-30 standard.

Annual prepay (option B) — mechanics:
- Invoice options: (i) 100% up-front prepay; (ii) 4x quarterly prepay; (iii) monthly prepay for 12 months (each invoice marked as prepaid).
- Discount applied at the contract level. Example: 12-month prepay, committed 20 GPUs -> 10% discount applied to committed spend.
- True-up cadence: quarterly. If quarterly usage > prepaid commit, overage billed on next invoice at overage rate; if usage < prepaid we apply credit to the following quarter.
- We can add a cost-exposure cap: overage cannot exceed 35% of prepaid committed spend in a given quarter without prior written approval.

Invoice language / PO details:
- Redwood will issue a consolidated invoice referencing the PO number. We accept emailed POs as countersigned purchase orders.
- Standard Net-30 on receipt of invoice; for larger deals we can extend Net-45 subject to credit review.
- Taxes: customer responsible; Redwood will provide tax documentation where required.

SLA / throughput: define target as p50/p95/p99 per-route; if we miss agreed p99 by >3% in a 30-day rolling window we'll credit X% of that month's committed spend (SLA doc attached).

Attaching the latest SLA doc that legal usually wants in the SOW. Happy to redline.

—Marissa
Senior Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement/architecture:

1) True-up frequency: quarterly reconciliation is acceptable, but we need clarity on how bursty usage is treated within the quarter. If we sustain >commit for a short 2–3 day spike, we’d rather not be billed at full overage for a temporary event. Any smoothing/window rules?

2) Overage cap: good to see a 35% cap by quarter — can we have an additional annual cap (e.g., no more than 100% of prepaid committed spend over the year) to limit worst-case exposure?

3) GPU SKUs: does the committed pool lock us to a GPU family (A100/H100) or can Redwood flex between SKUs based on availability? Pricing delta per SKU?

4) PO language: we will issue a single PO referencing the SOW and the order form. We normally require Net-45 for initial pilots; is that doable?

We want a short-contract option (6-month) and a 12-month with discount. If quotes are in line, we'll move to PO + SOW sign.

Best,
Sanjay

On another note — Mei and I will want a short model validation run to confirm throughput. Can Redwood stand up a 10-day verification window?

Hi Sanjay — quick finance perspective and proposed contract language you can give to procurement/legal:

- True-up calculation: monthly metering data aggregated into quarterly reconciliation windows. We compute committed vs actual consumption in GPU-hours adjusted by weighted token throughput (to account for variable token lengths). Spikes shorter than 7 days are smoothed into the quarter's usage by a rolling 7-day median to avoid penalizing brief bursts.

- Overage pricing: monthly reserved = 1.6x committed unit rate; annual prepay = 1.2x. We can cap charged overage to 35% of prepaid committed spend per quarter and 100% of prepaid committed spend per 12-month term if customer selects that clause. If you want a stricter annual cap (e.g., 50%), we can discuss credit offsets but that will reduce the prepay discount by ~2–3 percentage points.

- GPU SKUs: committed pool is expressed as equivalent GPU units (E-GPU). We guarantee SKU family at the time of order (e.g., H100) if you specify it in the SOW; otherwise Redwood reserves the right to supply equivalent SKU with equal or better performance. SKU-specific pricing: H100 ~ 20% premium vs A100 in committed pricing examples; we will show both on the quote.

- Net terms: Net-30 standard; Net-45 on initial pilot is acceptable pending internal credit approval. If you prefer Net-45 as contractual term, we require a signed PO referencing the contract and finance contact for billing.

- Invoice cadence & PO processing: Redwood will issue consolidated invoices referencing the PO. For 100% annual prepay we can split invoicing to match procurement needs (e.g., 50/50 upfront + 50% at 6 months) but discount applies to total prepaid amount.

I'll prepare suggested redlines for the SOW (true-up and caps) and share an example clause you can paste into procurement.

—Rishi
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

Sanjay — thank you. To keep momentum, proposed next steps and the commercial we can put on the table:

1) Commercial: 12-month annual prepay for committed pool (equivalent 24 E-GPUs / H100-class) with 10% contract-level discount. Overage: billed at 1.2x rate, quarterly true-up, 35% quarterly cap and 100% annual cap as discussed.
2) Invoice schedule: 50% upfront invoice within 7 days of countersigned PO; remaining 50% split into two quarterly prepay invoices (at month 4 and month 8) — Redwood will apply credits for any underutilization during quarterly true-up.
3) Net terms: Net-45 for the initial pilot accepted pending PO; regular renewals will move to Net-30.
4) Validation run: Redwood will provision a 10-day verification window on a small subset (4 E-GPUs) to validate throughput. We will define test routes, a success criteria doc, and schedule the run upon SOW sign-off.

If that aligns, we'll generate an order form and redlined SOW with the clauses Rishi mentioned. Expect the draft order form and SOW redline by EOD Wednesday.

Next steps: Sanjay to confirm commercial structure below and issue PO referencing DS-1347; Redwood to deliver draft order form + SOW redline.

—Jonas
